mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (إذا الشمس كورت): the discussion of the nominative of what follows (إذا) has already preceded, in al-Mursalāt and elsewhere.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t: His saying (مطاع ثم): (ثم) is an adverbial of place (ẓarf makān).

mekki-muskil:24-24.t:
His saying (على الغيب بضنين): the entry of (على) indicates that (ضنين) with ḍād means "miserly"; one says "I was miserly toward him" (بخلت عليه). Had it been with ẓāʾ [(بظنين)], meaning "suspected" [Translator's note: printed «منهم», read as «متهم»], it would have been with bāʾ, as one says "he is suspected of (بـ) such-and-such", and one does not say "of (على) such-and-such". (على) may also be in the place of the bāʾ, in which case the reading with ẓāʾ is good.
His saying (إلا أن يشاء الله): (أن) is in the position of the genitive with an implied bāʾ, or in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition.

mekki-muskil:26-26.t: His saying (فأين تذهبون): it should properly be with (إلى), because (ذهب) is intransitive; its implied form is "To where are you going?" But (إلى) was omitted, as they said "I went the Levant", i.e. to the Levant, and "I went out the market", i.e. to the market. Sībawayh reported of this only "I went the Levant", i.e. to the Levant, and "I entered the house", i.e. into the house. (أين) is an adverbial of place.
